questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Electrophilic nitration of indole under mild conditions (e.g., benzoyl nitrate) occurs selectively at
questions.explanationEn: In **indole**, electrophilic attack at **C3** produces a resonance-stabilized iminium ion that retains the full aromaticity of the fused benzene ring, whereas attack at C2 disrupts the benzene aromatic sextet in the key iminium resonance contributor. Thus, indole undergoes $\text{S}_\text{E}\text{Ar}$ selectively at **C3**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The decreasing order of resonance stabilization energy per ring among benzene, naphthalene, and anthracene is
questions.explanationEn: While total resonance energy increases with the number of fused rings (benzene $\approx 150\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, naphthalene $\approx 255\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, anthracene $\approx 351\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), the resonance energy **per ring** decreases: benzene ($150\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) $>$ naphthalene ($127.5\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) $>$ anthracene ($117\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The core tetracyclic carbon skeleton common to all steroids (such as cholesterol, testosterone, and progesterone) is
questions.explanationEn: All steroids share the fused 17-carbon tetracyclic core **cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene** (three 6-membered rings A, B, C fused to one 5-membered ring D). Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: According to Wallach's isoprene rule, a **sesquiterpene** has the carbon skeleton built from how many isoprene ($\text{C}_5$) units?
questions.explanationEn: Terpenes are classified by the number of $\text{C}_5$ isoprene units: monoterpenes = 2 ($\text{C}_{10}$), **sesquiterpenes = 3 ($\text{C}_{15}$)**, diterpenes = 4 ($\text{C}_{20}$), and triterpenes = 6 ($\text{C}_{30}$). Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Electrophilic nitration of naphthalene with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $50\,^\circ\text{C}$ occurs predominantly at
optionsEn: C1 and C2 in an exact $1:1$ ratio
questions.explanationEn: Electrophilic attack at C1 ($\alpha$-position) of naphthalene generates an arenium ion with **two** resonance contributors that retain an intact aromatic benzene ring, whereas attack at C2 ($\beta$-position) retains an intact benzene ring in only **one** contributor. Thus, 1-nitronaphthalene is the major kinetic product ($>90\%$). Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Mononitration of *p*-methylacetanilide (4-methyl-$N$-phenylacetamide) with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ occurs predominantly at which position?
optionsEn: in an equal $1:1$ mixture of C2 and C3
questions.explanationEn: When two activating groups compete on a benzene ring, the **stronger activating group** controls regioselectivity. The acetamido group ($-\text{NHCOCH}_3$, strong $+M$ resonance donor) activates the ring much more strongly than the weakly activating methyl group ($-\text{CH}_3$, hyperconjugation/$+I$). Since the *para* position to $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ is blocked by $-\text{CH}_3$, nitration occurs predominantly ***ortho* to $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$** (giving 4-methyl-2-nitroacetanilide). Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the **Strecker synthesis** of racemic alanine, acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) is treated with $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ and $\text{NaCN}$ to form an $\alpha$-aminonitrile intermediate, which upon acidic hydrolysis yields
questions.explanationEn: In the Strecker synthesis, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{NH}_3$ forms the planar imine $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{NH}$, which is attacked equally from both faces by $\text{CN}^-$ to give racemic 2-aminopropanenitrile. Acidic hydrolysis of the nitrile yields **racemic $(\pm)$-alanine**. Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: An aqueous mixture of aspartic acid ($\text{p}I = 2.77$), alanine ($\text{p}I = 6.00$), and lysine ($\text{p}I = 9.74$) is subjected to electrophoresis at $\text{pH } 6.0$. Which statement correctly describes the migration of the three amino acids?
optionsEn: Aspartic acid migrates toward the cathode ($-$), lysine toward the anode ($+$), and alanine remains near the origin
Aspartic acid migrates toward the anode ($+$), lysine toward the cathode ($-$), and alanine remains near the origin
All three migrate toward the cathode ($-$)
All three remain stationary at the origin
questions.explanationEn:
At $\text{pH } 6.0$:
- **Aspartic acid** ($\text{pH} > \text{p}I = 2.77$) carries a net **negative** charge $\implies$ migrates toward the **anode ($+$)**.
- **Alanine** ($\text{pH} = \text{p}I = 6.00$) is electrically neutral (zwitterion) $\implies$ remains near the **origin**.
- **Lysine** ($\text{pH} < \text{p}I = 9.74$) carries a net **positive** charge $\implies$ migrates toward the **cathode ($-$)**.
Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: When freshly dissolved in water, pure $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose ($[\alpha]_D = +112.2^\circ$) and pure $\beta$-D-glucopyranose ($[\alpha]_D = +18.7^\circ$) both equilibrate to a specific rotation of $+52.7^\circ$ (mutarotation). At equilibrium, $\beta$-D-glucopyranose predominates ($\approx 64\%$) over $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose ($\approx 36\%$) primarily because
optionsEn: the anomeric effect strongly favors the equatorial $-\text{OH}$ group

in the $^4C_1$ chair conformation of $\beta$-D-glucopyranose, all five non-hydrogen ring substituents (including the C1 $-\text{OH}$) occupy equatorial positions, minimizing 1,3-diaxial steric repulsions in water
$\alpha$-D-glucopyranose cannot form hydrogen bonds with water
$\beta$-D-glucopyranose exists exclusively in the open-chain aldehyde form
questions.explanationEn: In the $^4C_1$ chair conformation, **$\beta$-D-glucopyranose** has every bulky substituent—including the C1 $-\text{OH}$—in an **equatorial** orientation. In aqueous solution, water solvates the equatorial $-\text{OH}$ well and diminishes the stereoelectronic anomeric effect, making the sterically unencumbered $\beta$-anomer ($\approx 64\%$) thermodynamically favored over the axial $\alpha$-anomer ($\approx 36\%$). Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of phenanthrene with $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CCl}_4$ at room temperature gives predominantly 9,10-dibromo-9,10-dihydrophenanthrene (an addition product rather than substitution) because
optionsEn: the C9=C10 bond has high double-bond character, and addition across C9–C10 leaves two fully aromatic intact benzene rings (a biphenyl system) with minimal loss of resonance energy
bromine radicals attack C9 and C10 selectively
phenanthrene has no hydrogen atoms at C9 and C10
questions.explanationEn: In phenanthrene ($\text{RE} \approx 381\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), the $\text{C9}=\text{C10}$ bond is localized with high olefinic character ($\sim 80\%$ double-bond character). Addition across C9–C10 leaves a biphenyl-like system with two fully intact aromatic benzene rings ($2 \times 150 = 300\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), costing only $\sim 81\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ of resonance energy—far less than disrupting a benzene ring. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following disaccharides exhibit **mutarotation** in aqueous solution and give a positive **Fehling's test**?
questions.explanationEn: **Maltose**, **lactose**, and **cellobiose** all contain a $(1\to 4)$ glycosidic bond, leaving the second monosaccharide unit with a free anomeric hemiacetal ($\text{C1}-\text{OH}$) that equilibrates between $\alpha$, $\beta$, and open-chain aldehyde forms $\implies$ all three show mutarotation and reduce Fehling's reagent. **Sucrose** has a $(1\to 2)$ linkage locking both anomeric carbons $\implies$ non-reducing, no mutarotation. Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following reactions correctly synthesize the named heterocyclic ring system?
optionsEn: Fischer indole synthesis: arylhydrazone of an aldehyde or ketone + acid catalyst $\to$ substituted indole
Hantzsch synthesis: $\beta$-keto ester ($2\text{ equiv}$) + aldehyde + $\text{NH}_3$ (followed by oxidation) $\to$ substituted pyridine
Skraup synthesis: aniline + glycerol + conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ + nitrobenzene $\to$ isoquinoline
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Paal–Knorr thiophene synthesis uses a 1,4-diketone + $\text{P}_2\text{S}_5$.
- **(B) Correct:** Fischer indole synthesis converts arylhydrazones to indoles.
- **(C) Correct:** Hantzsch synthesis produces 1,4-dihydropyridines, which oxidize to pyridines.
- **(D) Incorrect:** The Skraup synthesis produces **quinoline**, not isoquinoline (isoquinoline is synthesized via the Bischler–Napieralski or Pomeranz–Fritsch synthesis).
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about peptide bonds and protein sequencing is/are correct?
optionsEn: The peptide bond ($-\text{CO}-\text{NH}-$) has partial double-bond character ($\sim 40\%$) due to amide resonance, restricting rotation and enforcing planarity.
Sanger's reagent (2,4-dinitrofluorobenzene) labels the $N$-terminal amino acid via nucleophilic aromatic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$).
In a tripeptide Gly–Ala–Val, glycine is the $N$-terminal residue and valine is the $C$-terminal residue by IUPAC convention.
Acid-catalyzed complete hydrolysis of a peptide ($6\text{ M HCl}$, $110\,^\circ\text{C}$, $24\text{ h}$) directly reveals the exact amino acid sequence without further methods.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Amide resonance imparts partial $\text{C}=\text{N}$ double-bond character and a planar *trans* geometry.
- **(B) Correct:** The free $N$-terminal $-\text{NH}_2$ displaces $\text{F}^-$ from FDNB via $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$.
- **(C) Correct:** Peptides are written from $N$-terminus (left) to $C$-terminus (right).
- **(D) Incorrect:** Complete hydrolysis determines only amino acid *composition*, not *sequence*.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about **furan** and **thiophene** is/are correct?
optionsEn: Furan acts as a conjugated diene in Diels–Alder cycloadditions with maleic anhydride, whereas thiophene does not under standard conditions.
In both furan and thiophene, one lone pair on the heteroatom is delocalized into the aromatic $\pi$-system while the second lone pair resides in an in-plane $sp^2$ orbital.
Thiophene is more stable toward mineral acids than furan.
Both furan and thiophene undergo electrophilic substitution preferentially at C3.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Furan has low aromatic stabilization energy ($67\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) and readily undergoes $[4+2]$ cycloaddition; thiophene ($121\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) resists Diels–Alder reaction.
- **(B) Correct:** Both $\text{O}$ and $\text{S}$ are $sp^2$-hybridized with one lone pair in $2p/3p$ (aromatic sextet) and one in $sp^2$.
- **(C) Correct:** Furan resinifies/hydrolyzes readily in strong mineral acid, whereas thiophene is acid-stable.
- **(D) Incorrect:** Both undergo $\text{S}_\text{E}\text{Ar}$ preferentially at **C2**.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of moles of phenylhydrazine ($\text{PhNHNH}_2$) consumed per mole of D-glucose to form D-glucosazone (along with $1\text{ mol}$ aniline, $1\text{ mol}$ $\text{NH}_3$, and $2\text{ mol}$ $\text{H}_2\text{O}$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Osazone formation consumes **$3$** moles of $\text{PhNHNH}_2$ per mole of aldose: $2$ moles are incorporated into the bis-phenylhydrazone at C1 and C2, while $1$ mole acts as an oxidant (being reduced to aniline and $\text{NH}_3$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of moles of acetic anhydride ($\text{Ac}_2\text{O}$) required to completely convert $1\text{ mol}$ of $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose into $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose pentaacetate is _______.
questions.explanationEn: $\alpha$-D-Glucopyranose possesses **$5$** free hydroxyl groups (at C1, C2, C3, C4, and C6). Complete acetylation therefore consumes **$5$** moles of $\text{Ac}_2\text{O}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For glycine, $\text{p}K_{a1} = 2.34$ (carboxyl) and $\text{p}K_{a2} = 9.60$ (ammonium). The isoelectric point ($\text{p}I$) of glycine is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: For a neutral amino acid without an ionizable side chain, $\text{p}I = \frac{\text{p}K_{a1} + \text{p}K_{a2}}{2} = \frac{2.34 + 9.60}{2} = \mathbf{5.97}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of isoprene ($\text{C}_5$) units in the sesquiterpene alcohol **farnesol** ($\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{26}\text{O}$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Farnesol contains $15$ carbon atoms, corresponding to $15 / 5 = \mathbf{3}$ isoprene units.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of open-chain stereoisomers possible for an **aldohexose** ($\text{HOCH}_2(\text{CHOH})_4\text{CHO}$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: An open-chain aldohexose has $4$ unsymmetrically substituted chiral centers (C2, C3, C4, C5), giving $2^4 = \mathbf{16}$ stereoisomers ($8$ D-aldohexoses and $8$ L-aldohexoses).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A double-stranded B-DNA sample is found by base-composition analysis to contain $22.0\text{ mol}\%$ adenine ($\text{A}$). According to Chargaff's rules, the mole percentage of **guanine ($\text{G}$)** in this DNA sample is _______ $\%$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn:
By Chargaff's rules for double-stranded DNA, $\%\text{A} = \%\text{T} = 22.0\%$, so $\%\text{A} + \%\text{T} = 44.0\%$.
The remaining $100.0\% - 44.0\% = 56.0\%$ is split equally between guanine and cytosine ($\text{G} = \text{C}$), giving $\%\text{G} = 56.0 / 2 = \mathbf{28.0}\%$.
